title: Will Trump Fire Powell?, Trump Softens Tone on China to Secure Xi Summit | Bloomberg The Pulse 7/17
content:
President Donald Trump said he’s not planning to fire Jerome Powell, and still managed to make it sound like a threat. Trump’s comments capped a hectic few hours that took his pressure campaign against the Federal Reserve chief to a new level — and sent markets into a shortlived nosedive. He ran the idea of sacking Powell by a group of Republican lawmakers late Tuesday. An aide said Wednesday morning he was likely to follow through. Then the president publicly backpedaled – with a major caveat. “I don’t rule out anything, but I think it’s highly unlikely, unless he has to leave for fraud,” Trump said.  Elsewhere, Trump has dialed down his confrontational tone with China in an effort to secure a summit with counterpart Xi Jinping and a trade deal with the world’s second-largest economy.

content: US retail sales rebounded in a broad advance, potentially tempering some concerns about a retrenchment in consumer spending.

title: US Initial Jobless Claims Decline for a Fifth Straight Week
content: Applications for US unemployment benefits declined for a fifth straight week to the lowest level since mid-April, showing a resilient job market.

title: Millions Wiped Off UK Debt as 239-Year-Old Agency Buys Gilts
content: Millions of pounds will be wiped off the UK’s debt stockpile after a two-centuries-old government body invested a gift from private donors into a gilt maturing this year.

title: Russia Notches Long-Awaited Win in Fight Against Inflation
content: Monthly price growth in Russia slowed significantly in June, the first meaningful sign that the central bank’s battle against inflation may be turning a corner after a protracted period of ultra-tight monetary policy.

title: Traders Target 1,000% Return With Bet on Deeper BOE Rate Cuts
content: Some traders have placed wagers in the UK options market that could net a more than 1,000% return if the Bank of England ignores inflation at an eighteen month high and delivers more cuts this year than rates pricing suggests.

title: G-20 Nearing Deal on Communique, South Africa Finance Chief Says
content: South African Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana said the Group of 20 advanced economies are nearing a deal on a communiqué.

title: Fed Independence Is a ‘Myth,’ JPMorgan’s Benhamou Says
content: The idea that the Federal Reserve operates free from political pressures is a “myth” and US stocks are likely to keep soaring on bets that interest rate cuts are coming, according to JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s Ilan Benhamou.

title: EU Proposes Joint Borrowing to Finance €400 Billion Crisis Tool
content: The €400 billion ($463 billion) crisis tool proposed by the European Commission on Wednesday would be financed using joint borrowing, according to people familiar with the matter.

content: Standing on the docks overlooking San Pedro Bay in Southern California, it’s hard for an outsider to tell where the Port of Long Beach ends and the Port of Los Angeles begins. But the cargo gateways that make up the Western Hemisphere’s largest maritime hub are distinct.

title: French Central Bank Chief Praises Plan to Fix ‘Very Excessive Deficit’
content: The French government’s contested plan to rein in the budget deficit goes in the right direction to tackle deep problems in public finances, the chief of the central bank said.

title: Currency Inflows to Russia Dwindle as Trade Shifts to Rubles
content: The flow of foreign currency into Russia is drying up as trade increasingly shifts to ruble payments, reflecting the impact of Western efforts to limit Russian cross-border transactions.

title: UK Jobs Hit from Reeves’ Budget Tax Hike Less Severe Than Feared
content: Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves’ first budget appears to have cost fewer jobs than previously estimated, casting fresh doubt over the state of the British labor market after a string of data issues in recent years.

title: G-20 Finance Chiefs Confront Growth Hit From Trump’s Tariffs
content: South Africa called for greater cooperation among the Group of 20 advanced economies, as finance ministers and central bank governors gathered under the cloud of US President Donald Trump’s trade war.

title: Germany Rejects EU Plan for Beefed-Up €2 Trillion Budget
content: Germany has rejected the European Commission’s proposal for a significantly expanded €2 trillion ($2.3 trillion) budget, just hours after it was announced by Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in Brussels.

title: EU’s Proposed €2 Trillion Budget Rejected by Germany
content: Germany has rejected the European Commission’s €2 trillion ($2.3 trillion) budget proposal, hours after it was announced by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in Brussels.

title: UK Unemployment Increases to 4.7%, Highest Rate in Four Years
content: Fresh jobs data reinforced a picture of a weakening British labor market, with unemployment notching up to the highest level in four years.

title: Indonesia to Continue Talks on Jets, Minerals After Tariffs Deal
content: Indonesia will keep talking with the US on sectoral tariffs, jet purchases and critical minerals after securing a 19% baseline tariff rate on exports to the world’s largest economy, a government adviser said Thursday.

title: South Korean Minister Nominee Says US Deal Possible in Two Weeks
content: South Korea’s foreign minister nominee said he believes it may be possible to reach a trade deal with the US before the 25% across-the-board tariffs proposed by President Donald Trump take effect in August.

title: Swiss Exports to US Rebound With Trump Trade Deal in Limbo
content: Swiss exports to the US rebounded in June, evidence that trade between the two countries remains robust despite the pressure of ongoing tariff negotiations.

title: Japan’s Opposition Parties Play Down Concerns Over Tax-Cut Plans
content: Japan’s opposition parties played down concerns over plans to cut taxes that have contributed to recent rises in bond yields ahead of Sunday’s upper house election.

title: Australian Unemployment at Four-Year High Bolsters Rate-Cut Case
content: Australian unemployment unexpectedly climbed to a four-year high in June as hiring almost stalled, suggesting a loosening of the labor market and bolstering the case for the Reserve Bank to reduce interest rates next month.

title: Trump Trade Deal Prods Garuda to Learn to Love 737 Max Again
content: Five months after a Boeing Co. 737 Max aircraft operated by Lion Air crashed into the Java Sea in 2018, Indonesian flag carrier PT Garuda Indonesia tried to cancel its remaining order for the same model. Now, the country is working to revive that deal as it seeks to forge favorable ties with US President Donald Trump’s administration.

title: UK Pushes US to Drop Key Sticking Point to Steel Trade Deal
content: UK officials are optimistic that the Trump administration will soon agree to modify the domestic-production requirements that are holding up a trade agreement to lower US tariffs on British steel.

title: Trump Raises Pressure on Powell While Calling Firing ‘Unlikely’
content: President Donald Trump said he’s not planning to fire Jerome Powell, and still managed to make it sound like a threat.

title: Japan’s Exports Fall as US Tariffs Stoke Recession Fears
content: Japan’s exports fell for a second month as US President Donald Trump’s tariff campaign continued to weigh on trade, further raising the risk of a technical recession for the nation’s sputtering economy.

title: Malaysia to Miss Fiscal Deficit Target This Year, BMI Says
content: Malaysia will likely miss its fiscal deficit target this year, as spending is seen exceeding projections and revenue may fall, according to BMI, a Fitch Solutions company.

title: Five Things to Watch in Commodities as China Targets Overcapacity
content: Involution, a state of hyper-competition that yields ever-diminishing returns, has become a buzzword for all that ails the Chinese economy — and a distinguishing feature of its commodities markets.

title: Williams Says Fed’s Restrictive Stance Is Entirely Appropriate

title: Ex-Lundin CEO Rockandel Joining Infor to Seize on Mining Deals
